text.content: A junior analyst on the team, unaware this was a test, forwarded the figure to a client-facing colleague who used it in a client briefing. When retrieval failed, the language model filled the gap with fabricated specificity.

text.content: Why prompt grounding matters

rich_text.plain_text: Why prompt grounding matters

text.content: Connecting a language model to a vector database does not automatically constrain it to that database. The model retains access to everything it learned during training. In the absence of a strict instruction, its default behaviour is to be helpful.

rich_text.plain_text: Connecting a language model to a vector database does not automatically constrain it to that database. The model retains access to everything it learned during training. In the absence of a strict instruction, its default behaviour is to be helpful.

text.content: This is the core tension in RAG system design. The retrieval pipeline is built to provide grounded evidence. But the language model will use that evidence only if it is explicitly instructed to do so and explicitly prohibited from doing otherwise. A weak instruction that says "use the documents" leaves open the possibility of supplementing them. A strong instruction that says "use only the documents and nothing else" closes that gap.

text.content: Takeaway:

rich_text.plain_text: Takeaway:

text.content: Retrieval and grounding are two separate problems that require two separate solutions. Retrieval is solved by the pipeline architecture (the vector store, the embedding model, and the Top K configuration). Grounding is solved by the system prompt.

rich_text.plain_text: Retrieval and grounding are two separate problems that require two separate solutions. Retrieval is solved by the pipeline architecture (the vector store, the embedding model, and the Top K configuration). Grounding is solved by the system prompt.

text.content: A well-configured retrieval pipeline connected to a weakly written system prompt is still an ungrounded agent. Both must be correct for the system to be trustworthy.
